tutorial.title: Logical Operators
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about logical operators and how we can use them to connect more than one conditions.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
With logical operators, we can connect two or more conditions to decide a result.

Start the game by connecting both the controller and game cartridge.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent: A logical operator connects the two conditions for the cartridge and controller to decide if the game must start or stay stopped.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
The AND operator && returns true only if all the conditions are true.

Make sure to type &&.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
The && operator will return false if one or more conditions are false. In the code, assign false to the doorUnlocked variable.

Make sure to type false.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
When operands and operators compute a boolean value together, it forms a logical expression, like hasKey && doorUnlocked.

Make sure to pick hasKey, followed by &&, and finally doorUnlocked.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
You can also store the result of a logical expression in a variable.

Make sure to pick let, followed by result, and finally =.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which logical operator gives us true if all the conditions are true?

&&!

Make sure to pick &&.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code print in the console?

truefalse

Make sure to pick false.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of the following is a logical expression?

playerAlive && hasContinueTokenscore + 10

playerAlive && hasContinueToken.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console for the result variable? true or false? Go through the code step by step to figure it out.

truefalse

Make sure to pick true.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Check if a player can enter a boss fight. Their level should be 18 or more and they should have a boss key.

Make sure to type &&.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Check if the player can craft a potion. For that, the player should have a bottle and the recipe should be unlocked.

Make sure to pick &&, followed by isRecipeUnlocked.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Store the logical expression in a const variable.

Make sure to pick const, followed by result, and finally =.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Store a logical expression in the canStartMatch variable that checks if the server is connected and the player is ready to start a match.

Make sure to type &&.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: We've seen that the AND operator requires all conditions to be true. But what if it's enough for only one condition to be true?

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent: For example, the gate here opens if the player has a key or the switch is on.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
For such conditions, we use the OR operator ||, which returns true as long as at least one of the conditions is true.

Make sure to type ||.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
If all the conditions are false, then the || operator returns false. Set the hasArmor variable to false.

Make sure to type false.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
We know that the NOT operator ! negates a boolean value. That means that it returns true if a condition is false and vice versa.

Make sure to type !.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use ! to negate logical expressions as well. To do that, we place the logical expression between parentheses.

Make sure to pick !, followed by (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
The logical expression returns false, but by negating it, we get true.

Make sure to type !.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which logical operator returns true if at least one of the conditions is true?

&&||

Make sure to pick ||.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

truefalse

Make sure to pick false.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which operator do we use to reverse the outcome of a logical expression?

&&!

Make sure to pick !.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of the following code snippets negates the logical expression?

!(condition1 && condition2)!condition1 && condition2

!(condition1 && condition2).

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

truefalse

Make sure to pick true.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Check if a player can enter the boss room depending on whether they have a boss key or their level is greater than the required level.

Make sure to pick ||, followed by >.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Save the opposite of isGameOver into the variable.

Make sure to type !.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Check if a player can start the next level or not.

Make sure to type =.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the || and ! operators to determine if a player can craft an item.

We do this by checking if any material is available or if the recipe list is not empty.

Make sure to pick ||, followed by !.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Save a game if cloud storage is greater than the save size or local storage is greater than the save size.

Make sure to pick >, followed by ||.
